ai.description: *Megophrys parva* is a small toad (35–45 mm) with a brown, leaf-patterned back. It features prominent, horn-like skin projections above the eyes and a distinct, dark-bordered triangular head marking.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Megophrys parva* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, elongated, horn-like tubercle on each upper eyelid, which is significantly more prominent than in other Indian congeners.
ai.habitat: *Megophrys parva* inhabits humid evergreen and subtropical broadleaf forests in the Himalayan foothills, typically at elevations between 600 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Concave-crowned Horned Toad is primarily nocturnal, remaining perfectly camouflaged among forest floor leaf litter to ambush passing insect prey.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Megophrys parva* breeds in streams during the monsoon (June–August), laying small clutches of unpigmented eggs attached to the undersides of submerged rocks.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Megophrys parva* occurs in the Eastern Himalayas and Northeast India, spanning states like West Bengal and Arunachal Pradesh at elevations between 1,000 and 2,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The *Megophrys parva* emits a short, high-pitched "peep" repeated at regular intervals, typically heard near small forest streams in mountainous habitats.
